_source: Which corpus artifacts realise each PRIMARY artifact of the docx register, and the declared schema for those nothing yet realises. Reviewable data, not inference: the docx names differ from the published ids, and a mapping guessed at publish time is one nobody can check. `tests/unit/scripts/test_artifacts_workbook.py` asserts every register row is accounted for here — mapped, or explicitly declared unrealised — so a new register row cannot be silently dropped.
_schema_sources: declared = a field list this repository actually states. `html` = the contract prose of the HTML artifact register. `code` = a module that reads the table and names its fields, which is the strongest kind: the reader and the schema cannot drift.

Business capability map.note: retired 18 Sep 2026 — step 5 matches the AI capability map, which is what the rest of the framework joins on. The licensed BA Guild maps are vector-mode and never files in this repository.

Traditional capability map.note: no schema declared anywhere — the contract names abstract TYPES (incident management, ERP, EHR, master data, identity...) but no per-row fields.

Traditional as-is architecture.note: the contract says 'same schema' as the AI as-is architecture.

Ontology.note: served by semantic-mcp (`semantic_ontologies`), not by the reference corpus — a tool, so it has no master to edit.

Grounding source classification.note: a classification OVERLAY on systems already inventoried, not a second estate list. `source-register` (32 rows) is adjacent but is not this.

Risk register.note: no schema declared — the contract says step-level risks map to enterprise entries, without naming the entry's fields.

Role rate registry.note: `lab.core.usecase.benefit._EFFORT_FIELDS` plus `role` — the module that reads the table names every field it requires, and refuses a row missing one.

Benefit benchmark library.note: partially realised — the drivers and formulas are published; the benchmark VALUES are not.

Delegation of authority matrix.note: `lab.core.usecase.authority.route` reads exactly these. With no table it ESCALATES and says why — routing money by a figure this lab invented is the one outcome it refuses. A live run escalated here on 13 Sep 2026.

outputs._note: Outputs are PRODUCED by a run, not supplied to it. They have no master to edit, so they appear in the index with the step that produces them and carry no sheet — the workbook is for artifacts the team provides.

framework._note: Published corpus artifacts that are NOT primary artifacts of the process: they describe the framework rather than supply it. Listed so every published id is accounted for — an unaccounted artifact is one nobody decided about.
framework.input-artifacts: the register of input artifacts itself
framework.output-artifacts: the register of output artifacts itself
framework.intake-fields: the Submit form's field groups, read by the review app
framework.intake-field-specs: the typed field specification behind that form
framework.business-case-sections: the eight sections step 24's business case must fill
framework.source-register: the lab's own source inventory — adjacent to the grounding source classification, and not it
